content.content:
=== comments
comments.py: his saved page comments that bear on an entry of POSITIONS.md.

    python3 -I comments.py 66            (or P-66)

He also comments on pages, and those comments are not in the transcripts. They are saved as
explorations/coordinator/positions-audit/evidence/curator-comments-*.md: a section per thread,
headed "## On <what it was anchored to>", with one bullet per comment, "- HH:MM: "words"".
A section counts when its heading, or a comment counts when its own words, either
  - name the entry's number, also as dictated: P-66, P66, PE66, P 66 (not P-660), or
  - quote its title: a quoted run ("..." or curly quotes) of at least three content words, at
    least 60 % of which are words of the entry's bold title (case, possessives and punctuation
    ignored).
A section that counts is printed whole, with its heading; a comment that counts in another
section is printed with that section's heading. Each with its file and line.

=== homes
homes.py: where a status that an entry of POSITIONS.md states may already live.

    python3 -I homes.py 151            (or P-151)
    python3 -I homes.py 151 --top 8    candidates per sentence (default 5)
    python3 -I homes.py 151 --at REV   the three files as commit REV holds them

Splits the entry (the working tree's POSITIONS.md; for an entry struck from it, its text as it
last stood, said so at the top) into sentences, and a sentence into its clauses
at the semicolons outside parentheses; a clause keeps the label that opens its sentence, as
"Built:" or "Still to build:". A clause states a status when it, its label or its sentence holds
one of the status words: built, to build, landed, pending, default, waits, standing go, listed for his
review, open, held, parked, owed, taken, stands at, returns after, not moved, and the like.

For each such clause it lists the candidates that may already hold the same point: the numbered
items of review-queue.md's lists (b) and (c), and the lines of PLAN.md (a numbered sub-line also
carries its parent's item number, and its own number as a fork when the parent counts forks).
A candidate is listed when it names the entry or shares a distinctive term with the clause:
  row N, item N (PLAN's), review-queue item N, fork N, way N, batch N, rung X, phase N, ask N,
  decision X, another entry's P-N, a name in backticks (a commit hash too), a dotted finding
  name such as judge-review.1 or A.skeptic.2
Each shared term weighs by its rarity among the candidates (log of the candidates over those
holding it); naming the entry adds 2; content words shared (four letters or more, beyond common
words) add a little, to order near-ties, and are printed apart. Candidates are ranked by that
weight, and each is printed with what it shares, for the scout to confirm or reject.

=== later
later.py: his messages after an entry's creation that may bear on it, though no commit of the
entry followed them (his later word may have gone into a skill or another record instead).

    python3 -I later.py 148                   (or P-148)
    python3 -I later.py 148 --top 25          how many to print (default 15)
    python3 -I later.py 148 --at 36f7db77c --until 2026-10-21T20:54
                                              the entry's text at a commit, and no message after a time

The candidates are his messages in the coordinating sessions (tlib.COORDINATING) from the entry's
creation on (for an entry struck from POSITIONS.md, its last text is read, and the list runs on
past the removal) (the first commit of its trail that made its text), less those that leads.py already
printed near the entry's own commits. Each is scored by the entry's distinctive terms:
  - its title's words, beyond common words (a stop list, and words in more than a tenth of his
    messages), lightly stemmed (possessive and plural off, cut to 7 letters); each weighs its
    rarity in his messages, log(messages / messages holding it);
  - its names in backticks, weight 3 each.
A term in his own words (lines that do not start with ">") counts whole; a term only in the
exchange around his message (the coordinator's message he answered, by the reply chain, its
reply to him, and the lines he quoted) counts half. A message also gains 8 when it falls in the
30 minutes before a commit that changed a file the entry names in backticks (`compiler.md`), other
than the entry's own commits, in lines that hold a title term (3 when the lines hold none): that
is where his word may have gone. Naming the entry's number (P-148, or as dictated, P148) adds 8 in
his words, 2 in the exchange. A message is a candidate when its weight is at least 5 (MIN) and it
holds a term in his own words or falls before such a commit. Printed: rank, weight, time, whether it
is after the entry's last change, the terms (in parentheses when only in the exchange), the commit
=== near
near.py: the curator's messages in a window before a UTC time, each with the coordinating
session's message that it answered, found along the transcript's reply chain.

    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z            window 60 minutes before the time
    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z 15m        or 2h, 1d
    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z 15m --cut 2000
                                                        cut each printed text at 2000 characters
                                                        (his and the coordinator's), saying so;
                                                        by default every text is printed whole

For each message of his: its time, source (main, s1, queued: see show.py), session, length and
full text. Then the message he answered: the coordinator's turn that his message follows on the
reply chain (tlib.py says how the chain is read), every text of that turn whole, each with its
time and the file and line it was read from (the first copy, when a resumed transcript replays
it). Before it, one line for each turn the chain passed over as not addressed to him (replies to
Stop-hook feedback, to an agent's message or hand-back, to a task notification or check-in, to a
system reminder), and for each text written after he sent his message; a passed-over turn that
answers a notification and ends with an ask to him (a question mark, "The ask", "I recommend",
"your yes", ...) is marked, and the newest such turn printed whole, since he may have answered
it. When he quotes lines ("> ..."), the text on the chain that holds them is named, and printed
whole if it is not the answer. After it, the last lines of the three turns to him further back
on the chain, for a message that answers an older question. A queued message (sent while a turn
ran) starts at its delivery into the turn; texts written after he sent it are not taken. A
message on no chain the index holds (a queued one never delivered) falls back to the time: the
coordinator's last text before it, passing over replies to Stop-hook feedback.
=== pointers
pointers.py: every line of the record that names an entry of POSITIONS.md by its number.

    python3 -I pointers.py 86            (or P-86)
    python3 -I pointers.py 86 --at REV   the files as commit REV holds them

Searches, at the working tree: explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, POSITIONS.md, PLAN.md,
review-queue.md, HELD.md and BOOT.md; explorations/reviews/open-asks-*.md; and every file under
.claude/skills/. The history files (POSITIONS-history.md, FACTS-history.md) are not searched:
trail.py reads the first, and both only record. A line counts when it holds the number as a word:
P-86 matches, as in "P-86's" or "(P-86)", but P-860 and P-186 do not. A line that names a range
holding the number ("P-85 to P-88") is listed too, marked as a range.
Prints path:line and the line (cut at 400 characters around the number; --whole prints it whole),
grouped by file; the entry's own line in POSITIONS.md is marked.

=== quote
quote.py: does the curator's message at a UTC time hold a quote word for word?

    python3 -I quote.py "QUOTE" 2026-09-26T10:21:32Z
    python3 -I quote.py "QUOTE" 2026-09-26T10:21        a prefix: every message of his in that minute

The time is a prefix of his message's timestamp, as show.py takes it (a trailing Z is dropped).
For each message of his at that time it prints one verdict:
  EXACT        the quote is a substring of the message as stored
  NORMALISED   a substring once both have every run of whitespace made one space, ends trimmed,
               and the curly apostrophe U+2019 made a straight one (nothing else is changed)
  NO MATCH     neither; it then prints the longest run of the quote's words that the
               message holds word for word (after the same normalising), for a reader to judge
With the match it prints the message's text around it.

=== trail
trail.py: the trail of one entry of POSITIONS.md, from the repository's history.

    python3 -I trail.py 86            (or P-86)
    python3 -I trail.py 86 --short    the commit list only, one line each
    python3 -I trail.py 86 --at REV   the record as commit REV holds it

Prints:
  1. the entry's text at HEAD (for an entry struck from POSITIONS.md: STRUCK at the top, with the
     commit that removed it and the reason its history block gives, and the text as it last stood);
  2. its blocks in POSITIONS-history.md at HEAD, each with the commit that wrote it (the oldest
     commit whose history file holds the block's provenance line). A block's own "commit X" names
     the source it cites, not its writer;
  3. every commit that made or changed the entry's text, oldest first, read from each commit's own
     tree (side branches included): hash, UTC author time, subject, what it did, how the link to
     the text before was made (number, line, title: exact; similarity: score printed), how many
     other entries of POSITIONS.md the commit changed, and the reasons on record: the history
     blocks it wrote, the comments above verbatim copies of the text in the old history file, and
     the commit message.
  4. a cross-check: the old history lines that the numbering block names as earlier texts of this
     entry, and whether each is a text of this trail.

What a commit did:
  created          a text new in POSITIONS.md that no removed or earlier text explains
  changed          a text that replaced another of the same commit (link: number, line, title or similarity)
  moved to history the text left POSITIONS.md and stands verbatim in POSITIONS-history.md
=== hischeck
hischeck.py: check the block of his quotes that a scout's or reader's report ends with.

per quote of his:
    HIS 2026-09-26T10:21:32.097Z | Run Fable judgement as well.
(a line may be wrapped in backticks or start with "- "). The time is a prefix of his message's
timestamp, as show.py takes it (a trailing Z dropped); each message of his at that time is tried,
and the quote is checked as quote.py does:
  EXACT        a substring of the message as stored
  NORMALISED   a substring once whitespace is collapsed and U+2019 made a straight apostrophe
  NO MATCH     neither, in every message at that time (quote.py "QUOTE" TIME shows the nearest run)
  NO MESSAGE   no message of his at that time
Lines of the block that start with HIS but do not parse are counted as BAD FORM. Prints, per
file, the counts and every line that is not EXACT or NORMALISED, with its line number; exits 1
when any line fails or a file has no block.

Nothing is filtered by author or by kind: a scheduled check-in or a pasted report that arrived as a

read along the transcript's reply chain (standard library).

live transcripts, the backup copies in /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded (the .parts folders
and the copy until 2026-10-08T15-41 included) and the first session on the `transcripts` branch;
deduplicated by uuid; queued messages with the time he sent them. load_msgs() rebuilds that list
from a per-file index (cache below) with show.py's own functions, in show.py's file order, so the
list is the same; tests.py checks it against show.load().

The message he answered (Talk.answered) follows the chain of the transcript itself: each line's
parentUuid (a compaction's logicalParentUuid), back from his message. Every line on the chain is
one of:
  his     a message of his (show.py's test), or his message queued while a turn ran, delivered
          into that turn (a queued_command attachment that is not a notification)
  text    an assistant line of the session (not a sidechain) holding text
  note    a prompt that is not his: Stop-hook feedback, an agent's message or hand-back, a task
          notification (also a scheduled check-in), a system reminder, a prompt starting '<'
  pass    everything else, passed through: tool calls and results, attachments, hook summaries,
          and the prompts that only continue a turn (a compaction summary, "Continue from where
          you left off", a worker restart notice, a skill's text, an image, a local command)
Going back from his message, the texts met are collected; reaching a note drops them as a turn
not to him (they are listed as skipped), and reaching a prompt of his makes them the answer: the
coordinator's whole turn after that prompt, every text of it, oldest first. A text written after
he sent his message (a queued message is delivered late) is listed apart, not taken. The turns to
him further back on the chain are kept too (Talk.answered(..., earlier=3)), for a reply to an
older question. Two checks on the rule: a skipped turn that answers a notification and ends with
an ask to him (ASK: a question mark, "The ask", "I recommend", "your yes", ...) is marked 'asks',
since the coordinator often relays an agent's result with a question; and when his message
quotes lines ("> ..."), the newest text on the chain that holds them is found ('quoted').
Talk.reply(m) gives the coordinator's turn after his message m.

Cache: ./cache/tx3-<path hash>.pickle, one per transcript file, holding the file's index and its

**`label` is not a goto.** It's a named block that code inside it can leave early, with a value. Rust's labelled `break` with a value and Scala's `boundary`/`break` are the nearest equivalents.

```
label search
  ...
  exit search with x   (leaves the block; the block's value is x)
  ...
end search
```

`exit` can only jump to the end of a `label` that encloses it, never anywhere else. If no `exit` runs, the block's value is its last expression.

**The expected type.** Yes, Fortress works like Scala and Swift here: a block's value is its last expression, and a function's body is that expression.
- The checker carries "the type this spot needs" down into an expression. A function body gets its declared return type, and the block passes it on to its last expression.
- This matters for one kind of function. In `fail[\T\](s: String): T`, `T` appears only in the result, so the arguments can't fix it. Only the expected type can.
- Example: in `x: ZZ32 = fail("bad")`, `T` becomes `ZZ32`.
- Where nothing is expected, `T` falls back to its bound, `Any`.

**`typecase`, and what batch 11's Q2 decided.**
- `typecase v of A => e1; B => e2 end` picks a branch by `v`'s run-time type.
- Its type is the union of its branches' types, so each branch gets the type the whole `typecase` is expected to have.
- Q2 asked whether a call inside a branch gets that expected type. The batch made it so.

    typecase baseString of

end methodVerify

**The team's indexing:**
- Every index type in their tree is `ZZ32`, a pair or triple of `ZZ32`, or a generic `I` passed through. Nothing else.
- Every range they built since 2008 took integers. Their specification calls a range "a set of integers".

- Swift's opaque `String.Index` is the one design Fortress never had. Swift, Scala and Julia all keep lookup by key apart from indexing by position.

**What your decision changed:**
- **Removed:** ranges over `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` and `ZZ`, and mixed widths in 2-D and 3-D ranges.
- **Left generic:** `Indexed`, the array traits, the public range traits and the maps.

- (c) narrows only `(:)` used as a range value in 2-D and 3-D, which no team code does. It also gives up the team's wildcard type `Any`.

## 5. Q49 after probe P3

This point reads main at `8e276cf48`, and its line numbers are that commit's.

**Words used below.**
- A **value**: walk runs the program and prints a result.
- A **stop**: the run ends with an error instead.
- A **checker site**: one place in the library that the checker refuses. The **distance** counts them. It must reach zero before the compiled path can use the interpreter's library.

**What `(:)` is.**
- `(:)` is the open range: a range that means "everything". A bare `#` builds it too, so `a[#]` is `a[:]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4036-4037`).
- It is one object, `TrivialOpenRange` (`:3883-3906`).
- That object extends `OpenRange[\Any\]`. So it is a range whose index type is `Any`, the type that holds every value.
- The team used `Any` as a wildcard: "whatever the index type". `(:)` was a value of type `OpenRange[\Any\]` before 2008 (`7c1b30b2b:Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2002-2003`), and Maessen's rewrite made it this object (`0948c2b1c`, 2008-10-07; `0948c2b1c:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3104`).
- It has two jobs:
  - **the subscript marker**: `a[:]` is all of `a`, and `m[:, j]` is column `j` of `m`;
  - **a range value**: a program can also compare it, test membership in it, or cut it, like any other range: `(:) CMP (:)`, `3 IN (:)`, `(:).truncL(3)`.

**The five methods.**
- Every range must provide them, because the trait `Range[\I\]` declares them (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2172-2178`). A range over `ZZ32` provides them at `I = ZZ32`.
- What each does, with what walk printed for `(:)` before climb batch 12 (`compile-ladder/rung-range-kinds/REPORT.md:187-191`):
  - `truncL(x)` keeps the indices at or after `x`. `(:).truncL(3)` was `LeftScalarRange(3,1)`, the range `3#`: 3, 4, 5 and on.
  - `truncR(x)` keeps those at or before `x`. `(:).truncR(3)` was `RightScalarRange(3,1)`, the range `:3`.
  - `every(s)` keeps every `s`-th index. `(:).every(3)` was `OpenScalarRange(3)`, the range `::3`.
  - `imposeStride(s)` does the same on `(:)`: `(:).imposeStride(3)` was `OpenScalarRange(3)` too.
  - `atMost(k)` keeps at most `k` indices. `(:).atMost(3)` was `ExtentScalarRange(3,1)`, the range `#3`: three indices, not yet placed.
- The team's bodies built these with the range operators: `(x#)`, `(:x)`, `(::x)`, `(::x)` and `(#k)` (`720ef21e4:Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3873-3879`).

**Why the checker cannot type them.**
- `(:)` is a range over `Any`, so it inherits each method at `I = Any`. Each takes an `Any` and must answer a range over `Any`, for example `truncL(x:Any): RangeWithLeft[\Any\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3887`).
- Fortress generics are invariant. A range over `ZZ32` is not a range over `Any`, though every `ZZ32` is an `Any`. Fortress has no mark like Scala's `+T` that would allow it.
- The range operators take only a `ZZ32`, or a pair or triple of them, and answer a range over that type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2281-2339`). So `(x#)` with `x` an `Any` fits none of them. The checker says so at each of the five: "Could not check call to operator # - (ZZ32, ZZ32)->LeftRange[\(ZZ32, ZZ32)\] is not applicable to an argument of type Any" (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:96`).
- The library has no range over `Any` to answer with. So the only body the checker can accept is one that answers nothing: a `fail`.
- Walk has no static types. It looked at the value at run time, `3`, chose the `#` over `ZZ32`, and answered.

**When the five are called.**
- Only when code calls one of them on a value that is `(:)`. There are two ways to do that:
  - directly: `(:).truncL(3)`;
  - through generic range code, written for any range. The library has two such operators: `r:s`, with a range `r` on the left, calls `r.imposeStride(s)`, and `r#n` calls `r.atMost(n)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4125`, `:4130`). So `(:):3` and `(:)#3` reach them.
- The library's subscripts never call them. Each takes `(:)` by its own type, `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1298`, `:1379`, `:1419`, `:1446`, `:1466`, `:1555`, `:1588`, `:1693`, `:1824`), and does something else:
  - the generic `a[:]` asks for `openRange[\I\]()`, an open range at the indexed value's own index type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1883`);
  - a `ZeroIndexed` value, such as a string, a list or a set, answers itself (`:1913`);
  - `a[:] := b` assigns over `a`'s bounds (`:1988`);
  - the arrays of rank 1 to 3 answer a subarray of the whole (`:2259`, `:2317`, `:2540`, `:2951`);
  - `m[:, j]` and `m[i, :]` read a column or a row (`:2561`, `:2565`).
- The range kinds call the five only on themselves, on their own parts, which are scalar ranges over `ZZ32`, or on another scalar range (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:218-341`, `:367-370`, `:462`, `:608-616`, `:697-699`, `:866-868`, `:1041-1043`). `(:)` is none of those.
- I searched the 2,392 tracked `.fss` and `.fsi` files outside `explorations/` and `research/`: the library, the compiler's own library, the demos and every test folder. `(:)` appears in nine files, and `(#)`, `(:):` and `(:)#` in none:
  - the library: the five `fail` messages, and QuickCheck's `genRange` (below);
  - `ProjectFortress/tests/RangeDeclarations.fss:122`, `(:) CMP (:)`, and `RangeNarrowKinds.fss:39`, `(:).narrowToRange(:)`; neither calls the five;
  - the five tests `ProjectFortress/tests/TrivialOpenRange{TruncL,TruncR,Every,ImposeStride,AtMost}Stop.fss`, which climb batch 12 wrote to pin way (a)'s stops.
- The subscripts written with a bare `:` or `#`, such as `x0[:]`, `g[#]`, `a2[1,:]` and `a2[:,2]` (`Library/Tuple.fss:30`, `Library/List.fss:194`, `ProjectFortress/tests/subArray.fss:80-81`), go to the subscripts above, by reading.
- So no library, test or demo code calls the five on `(:)`, apart from those five tests. Before climb batch 12, none did.

**QuickCheck's `genRange`.**
- `object genRange[\I\](genI:Gen[\I\]) extends Gen[\Range[\I\]\]` makes random ranges for testing (`Library/QuickCheck.fss:491`). Its `generate` answers `(:)` one time in 32, as a `Range[\I\]` (`:494-496`).
- The team's comment above it: "Mostly for the testing of subscripts. (XXX not tested)" (`:490`). No code in the tree subscripts with its ranges.
- One caller names it: the library's default `Arbitrary`, for any `Range[\I\]` (`:732-733`, called from `:763`). One gated test reaches it that way, at `ZZ32`, and prints four draws (`ProjectFortress/tests/QuickCheckTest.fss:67`). Its `perturb` reads a range's `stride`, `left` and `right` (`:506-510`), not the five.
- This note said before that way (c) would make the `(:)` line type. That was wrong. P3 found that it types under neither (a) nor (c) (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:116`).
- Why: the checker checks `generate` once, for every `I` at once, without knowing `I`. The line must answer a `Range[\I\]` for that unknown `I`.
  - Under (a) and (b), `(:)` is a `Range[\Any\]`. By invariance, that is a `Range[\I\]` only when `I` is `Any`.
  - Under (c), it is a `Range[\ZZ32\]`: a `Range[\I\]` only when `I` is `ZZ32`.
  - Neither fits an unknown `I`. That the one test uses `ZZ32` does not help: the checker does not check each use on its own.
- By reading, `generate`'s three other branches do not type at an unknown `I` either: `:` takes only a `ZZ32` or a tuple of them (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2285-2306`).
- `QuickCheck` is also not among the twelve components that the distance measures (`coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh:83-85`). So `genRange` counts for none of the three ways.

**What each way means for a program you write.**
- Main runs way (a). Climb batch 12 built it as Q49's default (`abe8b0342`; PLAN item 49). POSITIONS now records it, "The open range `(:)` keeps its wildcard type, and its five cutting methods fail", an entry that ends "his confirmation after `explorations/reviews/ranges-and-index-types.md` and P3" (`8e276cf48`).
- Keeping (a) changes nothing on main. Choosing (b) or (c) instead removes the five `fail` bodies and their five tests. Under (b) the five checker sites come back. Under (c) the five bodies change type, and the checker's view of them is not measured.
- P3 compared walk's values on the library from before climb batch 12 (`fe74fb738`) with way (c). "Before" below means that library.

**(a) `fail` bodies** (on main).
- Example: `(:).truncL(3)`. Before, walk printed `LeftScalarRange(3,1)`. Now the run stops: "truncL of the trivial open range (:), whose index type is Any". The same holds for the other four, and for `(:):3` and `(:)#3`, which call two of them (`compile-ladder/rung-range-kinds/REPORT.md:187-193`).
- By reading, the same at pairs and triples: `(:).truncL((1,2))` stops too, since the body is a `fail` whatever its argument.
- The way edits only the five bodies. So the subscripts by `(:)`, `3 IN (:)`, `(1,2) IN (:)` and `(:) CMP (:)` are untouched.
- The five checker sites clear (FACTS, "The one library's `narrowToRange` and its bounds check are declared at the range kinds over `ZZ32` of rank 1 to 3").
- `(:)` stays a range "whatever the index type", as the team made it. A `fail` is the library's own way for a body that cannot answer its declared type (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:98`), and (a) is the record's recommendation (`:106`).

**(b) Leave the team's bodies.**
- Example: `(:).truncL(3)` prints `LeftScalarRange(3,1)` again. The five, `(:):3` and `(:)#3` answer as before climb batch 12, at every rank.
- The five checker sites stay. The checker can never accept them as written (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:104`), so the distance cannot reach zero while they stand (`:101`).

**(c) `(:)` as a range over `ZZ32`.**
- The library change: `TrivialOpenRange extends OpenRange[\ZZ32\]`, and the five take a `ZZ32`, with the team's bodies.
- Its `INTERSECTION`, `=`, `IN` and `CMP` must move to `ZZ32` too. Without them walk refuses the library: "Invalid overloading of CAP in TrivialOpenRange" (`CAP` is another name of `INTERSECTION`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser_util/precedence_resolver/Operators.java:1322`).
- By reading, `stride` must change too, from `()` to `1`: every range's `stride` is of its index type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2164`), and the checker reads that (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:116`).
- P3 ran 186 programs of one expression each under walk, on the library from before and on (c). 64 differ:
  - **25 values become stops**, all at a pair, a triple or a string:
    - the five at rank 2 and 3 (10): `(:).truncL((1,2))` was `LeftRange2D(1,2, 1,1)`, and `(:).every((2,2,2))` was `OpenRange3D(2,2,2)`;
    - `(1,2) IN (:)`, `(1,2,3) IN (:)` and `"x" IN (:)`, which were `true` (3);
    - `(:) << (1,2)`, `(:).shiftRight((1,2))` and the same at rank 3, which were `(:)` itself (4);
    - the generic `:` and `#` on `(:)` with a pair or a triple, which were `OpenRange2D(2,2)`, `ExtentRange2D(4,4, 1,1)` and the same at rank 3 (4);
    - generic code that takes `(:)` as a `Range[\I\]` at a pair or triple `I`, and calls `x IN r` or `r.truncL(x)` (4).
  - **16 stops become values**, all at rank 1 with `(:)` on the left:
    - `(:) INTERSECTION r` answers `r`, for seven kinds of scalar range `r` (7);
    - `(:) CMP r` answers `GreaterThan`, or `EqualTo` for `::1` and `::2` (7);
    - `(:) FORWARD_CMP (0#3)` answers `GreaterThan`, and `(:).narrowToRange(0#3)` answers `0#3` (2).
    - Before, these stopped with "Failed to find any matching overload": the object's operators take a range over `Any`, and no range over `ZZ32` is one. No ledger row records that.
  - **16 stops stay stops**, with another error: at rank 1 with `(:)` on the right, `r INTERSECTION (:)`, `(0#3).narrowToRange((:))` and `r CMP (:)` (15), and `genRange`'s `perturb((:), g)` (1).
  - **7 values change**: `(:).left`, `.right` and `.extent` print `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` for `Nothing[\Any\]` (3); `(:)` becomes an instance of `Range[\ZZ32\]` and `OpenRange[\ZZ32\]`, and stops being one of `Range[\Any\]` and `OpenRange[\Any\]` (4).
- **Unchanged:** every subscript by `(:)` (`a[:]`, `a[:] := b`, `m[:]`, `m[:, 1]`, `m[1, :]`, `"hello"[:]`, a list's `[:]`); the five at rank 1, so `(:).truncL(3)` is `LeftScalarRange(3,1)`; `3 IN (:)`; `(:)` with itself; `INTERSECTION`, `=` and `CMP` of `(:)` with ranges of rank 2 and 3.
- The interpreter's suites, `ant testSystem`, pass on (c): 526 tests, 0 failures. No team test moves.
- With `stride` at `1`, measured on a third copy of the library:
  - `(:).stride` is `1`, where it was `()`;
  - the seven `r CMP (:)` stops become values, `LessThan` (`EqualTo` for `::1`), so 23 values are gained in all;
  - `(::1) = (:)` becomes `true`, while `(:) = (::1)` stays `false`. So `=` answers differently by side: `::1` compares strides (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:366`), while `(:)` asks whether the other is `(:)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3902`).
- Not measured: the checker under (c). By reading, the five bodies type at `ZZ32` (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-12.md:116`).

**So what you decide.**
- Not indexing. Every subscript by `(:)` works the same under all three ways. P3 measured that for (c); (a) and (b) do not touch the subscripts' code.
- Not the `ZZ32` decision. No way reverts it, and none needs it reverted.
- Only what `(:)` does as a range value, in a program that cuts, strides or compares it. No code in the tree does that through the five, apart from the five tests that pin way (a).

  - (b): the five methods answer as before, at every rank. The five checker sites stay, and the checker can never accept them.
  - (c): `(:)` becomes a range over `ZZ32` only. The five answer at rank 1 only. 25 values at pairs, triples and strings become stops, 16 uses at rank 1 of its `INTERSECTION`, `CMP`, `FORWARD_CMP` and `narrowToRange` that stopped before start working (23 with `stride` at `1`), and 7 values print differently. ### Q50. Item 50: the bounds check of a range of rank 2 or 3, row 657, a value walk prints

- **Blocks:** no site. Rung R clears row 655's 2 sites either way; your answer decides the value.
- **On file:** PLAN item 50; rows 655 and 657; rung L's decision 6 and section 10; today's value pinned at `ProjectFortress/tests/RangeKindBodies.fss:94`. Rung L recommends the repair.
- **Terms.** `r.narrowToRange(other)` is the part of `other` inside `r`, and it raises `IndexOutOfBounds` when `other` reaches outside `r`; `checkSelection` (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:125-138`) is that check. A bound of a rank-2 range is a pair. Lexicographic order compares the first components, then the second on a tie. Point by point compares each component on its own axis; `PCMP` (`RangeInternals.fss:113`) does that.
